candidates.excerpt: In episode 6 of the TrainsPRO Podcast, Trains Magazine Editor Bill Stephens sits down with intermodal analyst Larry Gross, president and founder of Gross Transportation Consulting. They discuss intermodal’s record year, the growth targets in the proposed Union Pacific–Norfolk Southern merger, and the threat autonomous trucks pose to rail. Gross has more than 40 years of experience in freight transportation, including 27 years at Wabash National, and writes the monthly Landlines column in the Journal of Commerce. What’s driving intermodal’s record year U.S. intermodal is on pace to top its 2018 record. Gross says it’s important to separate intermodal into its two very different markets. International moves ocean containers inland from ports, while domestic moves mostly 53-foot containers. Overall volume is up 3.4% year to date. candidates.excerpt: WASHINGTON — Two organizations representing major auto manufacturers have told the Surface Transportation Board they oppose the Union Pacific-Norfolk Southern merger, saying it will reduce competition at gateways and expose automakers to increased pricing power, equipment shortages, and service disruptions. The joint filing from the Automotive Logistics Executive Committee (ALEC) and the Alliance for Automotive Innovation (AAI) paints a dire picture of other railroads’ ability to compete without further merger activity, while saying the impact on shippers of a system with two transcontinental railroads remains unaddressed. They do not propose any conditions if the merger is approved, saying there are “limited options” to mitigate the harms of the transaction. A separate filing from General Motors outlines some of the same concerns but does not support or oppose the merger. candidates.title: Model railroad safety tips
candidates.excerpt: Full-size railroads constantly promote safety to their employees. Signs on buildings and in shops and slogans on locomotives, freight cars, and (back in the day) cabooses are all intended to keep safety at the front of mind. Though model railroading is considerably less dangerous than professional railroading, it’s not without hazards. Chemicals in the various paints and glues we use, sharp blades in hobby knives, and power tools used for building benchwork are just a few examples of items that can potentially cause injury. In this article we’ll discuss some model railroad safety tips. Though many of the tips here focus on personal workshops and layouts, safety is also important if you’re hosting work nights, operating sessions, and open houses. Have a briefing to show guests where exits are located and where first aid kits, flashlights, fire extinguishers, fire blankets, and other safety items are stored. candidates.title: PIL and Qingdao Port complete China’s first bio-LNG bunkering for international shipping
candidates.excerpt: Pacific International Lines (PIL) and Qingdao Port have completed what they describe as China’s first liquefied bio-methane (LBM) bunkering operation for an internationally trading vessel. The operation took place at Qingdao Port’s QQCTN terminal, where PIL’s LNG dual-fuel containership Kota Odyssey received ISCC-certified LBM through a truck-to-ship transfer. It also marks the Singapore-based carrier’s first use of the renewable fuel in its fleet. Produced from organic feedstocks, LBM, also known as bio-LNG, can be used in LNG dual-fuel engines without modifying the vessels’ existing machinery. PIL is introducing the fuel as part of its efforts to reduce shipping emissions while expanding its fleet of dual-fuel containerships. According to the carrier, the batch supplied at Qingdao is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by more than 70% compared with conventional fuel oil, based on a well-to-wake lifecycle assessment. candidates.excerpt: The Port of Oakland and WattEV, a leading provider of heavy-duty charging infrastructure, have opened a new heavy-duty electric truck charging depot at the port, the first of its kind in Northern California. Officials also announced the purchase of 300 electric Tesla Semi trucks to serve the port, with the first batch due before the end of the year and the balance in 2027. According to WattEV, at current high diesel prices the operating costs of these electric trucks are half those of comparable diesels. The trucks will help establish a zero-emission freight corridor from the Bay Area to Sacramento, the Central Valley, Nevada and beyond, and the depot forms part of the port’s continued electrification. The depot, at 8407 Edgewater Drive, can charge 25 medium- and heavy-duty electric trucks at once at up to 240 kW each, or seven trucks at 1.2 MW. candidates.title: The Hidden Economics of Dedicated Logistics Networks
candidates.excerpt: A container’s journey does not end when a vessel reaches port. After discharge, it must move through a terminal, reach an inland destination by road, rail or barge, and eventually return to a depot or find another export load. Each transfer creates costs and operational dependencies. For shipping lines and cargo owners, the economics of this journey increasingly depend on how efficiently the different assets and operators work together. Dedicated logistics networks offer one way to coordinate these movements. They connect container terminals, inland depots, transport capacity, empty-container facilities and digital systems through company-owned assets, long-term partnerships or reserved third-party capacity. The objective is to improve control over container flows while making transport and infrastructure resources more productive. candidates.excerpt: Port of Gothenburg invests in electrified rail access to the container terminal The Port of Gothenburg is investing in overhead line infrastructure for the container terminal’s handling tracks in a move that will boost capacity, cut emissions and improve the efficiency of rail operations. The investment will enable electric locomotives to run directly to and from the terminal, removing the need for diesel locomotives or detours via the port departure yard. The project is designed to create more efficient rail flows within the port area and support continued growth in rail freight volumes. By extending the overhead line infrastructure to the container terminal’s handling tracks, electric locomotives will be able to operate all the way to and from the terminal. This will reduce the need for shunting via the port departure yard, freeing up capacity, shortening turnaround times and lowering carbon emissions.
